tasks.task: Check this period's payroll inputs before the run

items.when: Every pay period, to run the steps from change cut-off to the client pressing run
When this period's inputs must be checked person by person against last period
When several source files feed payroll and you need an exception list tied back to each
When two exports should list the same people, to find unmatched rows and duplicate keys
When the run is large, to flag odd amounts with a short reason for each
When totals moved since last period and each line past the limit needs a written reason

tasks.task: Check timesheets against hours, overtime and break rules

items.when: Before payroll, to test every timesheet against the client's own written rules
When raw timesheets need hours totalled by person and every oddity flagged for approval
When the export has text numbers, mixed dates or duplicates that would break the check
When a flagged entry turns on an overtime or break rule and you need the rule with its source

tasks.task: Build the change log of starters, leavers and pay changes

items.when: Before each cut-off, to list every change with who approved it and when it starts
When changes arrive by chat and email and managers need one form with set fields
When the log must be matched to the staff list to catch a missing leaver or a double entry

tasks.task: Reconcile payroll totals to the bank and the ledger

items.when: When net pay on the register must match what left the bank, with gaps sorted by type
When the payroll journal or an accrual needs debits, credits and support for review
When holiday pay or bonuses earned but unpaid need an accrual schedule
At month end, to find payroll accounts that do not reconcile and odd entries

tasks.task: Answer staff pay questions from the firm's own policies

items.when: When staff keep asking about overtime, leave pay, sick pay or payday
When the answer must come from the handbook in plain words
When the policy is silent and you need the outside rule with its source to flag for review
Before replying, to check each line points to a written policy or a dated official source

tasks.task: Build pay bands the business can explain

items.when: When roles need levels, midpoints from dated market data and written movement rules
When bands, bonus and benefits are all being set together in one run
When you need public pay ranges for a role and place before setting a midpoint
When you hold market data for one role and need a range with a method leaders can follow
When the firm has no job levels yet and bands need something to hang on
Before sharing, to tie every market figure to a named and dated source

tasks.task: Run a fair-pay check across similar roles

items.when: When each person must be placed in a band and gaps between like roles explained
When you first get the pay file, to see missing values and odd entries before any maths
When current pay must be set against market ranges and outliers listed
When you need to know if a gap between groups is real or just a small sample
When the team is large enough to test a pay gap after level, tenure and place
When a gap has a reason on paper and you must ask whether the rule itself is fair

tasks.task: Run the annual pay review

items.when: Eight to ten weeks before new pay starts, to set the steps, data and sign-offs
When the review budget must be shown by team and month for finance
When the budget is fixed, to compare two ways to split it with money and dates
When a raise depends on a promotion and the evidence must be matched to the criteria
Before leaders see the review sheet, to find formula errors and totals that do not tie

tasks.task: Build a fair one-page case for a pay raise

items.when: When an employee or manager needs a case built from results, scope and named market data
When the person also needs a script and replies to the likely answers
When the talk may get tense and they need an opening, questions and a fallback
Before it is handed over, to tie each result and market figure to a source

tasks.task: Cost a benefits plan at three budget levels

items.when: When the owner wants options with cost per person and in total before talking to a broker
When benefits must sit in one plan with pay grades and a bonus formula
When a benefits or payroll provider must be chosen on weighted criteria
Before the costing goes to the owner, to find broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Write a total pay statement staff can follow

items.when: When staff should see pay, bonus and benefits in one statement outline
When a figure needs one small traced example so people can check their own
Before it goes out, to read the statement as an employee and list what they cannot follow

tasks.task: Design a sales commission plan for one role

items.when: When one sales role needs on-target pay, quota from real capacity, rates and deal rules
When the plan is being set along with who to hire and what early success looks like
Before settling the split, to compare two differently shaped plans with the money shown
When the draft is ready, to see who is rewarded for what and where it pulls the wrong way
Before launch, to trace what reps will do next and three signs to watch
When the plan pays on signing and ignores whether customers stay
When you need to turn the plan upside down and ask how a rep would game it

tasks.task: Model commission payouts in three scenarios

items.when: When payouts at low, target and high results must be shown with the maths
When quota looks like a guess and you need to see what the pipeline can really support
When the model is built, to have the figures recalculated and the key assumption named
Before sharing the workbook, to list formula errors and broken links
When you have past deal data and want quick tables and charts of who would have earned what

tasks.task: Write the commission plan document reps can read

items.when: When the plan is agreed and each rep must be able to check it against their payslip
When a rule needs one worked deal with traced numbers
When the document reads like a contract and reps will skip it
Before reps sign, to read it as a rep and list every place two readings are possible

tasks.task: Review a commission plan that is not working

items.when: When you have the plan and churn by rep and need what it rewards, ignores and one change to test
When the people who wrote the plan also gain from it
When sales, support and finance are paid to want different things
When more commission is the only fix on the table and the real issue may be elsewhere

tasks.task: Design a team bonus or recognition plan

items.when: When the firm wants a reward anyone can win by reaching a set level
When a bonus needs a payout formula and its cost against budget
Before launch, to see what the bonus really rewards
When the plan is all money and no moment of being seen

tasks.task: Build an offer package inside the pay bands

items.when: When a candidate has asked for more and you need a package and a negotiation plan
When the offer includes share options and the grant needs modelling
Before the letter goes, to flag risky pay terms for the place of work

tasks.task: Set up payroll for a first hire or a new provider

items.when: When a first hire is starting and the owner needs dated tasks and accountant questions
When payroll software is being chosen and vendors must be compared on the same tasks
Before someone is added to payroll or paid by invoice, to flag the status risk
Before a system switch, to check who will see pay data

tasks.task: Write the payroll calendar and pay-run procedure

items.when: When the cut-off, checks and sign-offs need fixed days in every period
When the pay run must fit the close, with dated tasks, owners and blockers
When only one person knows how payroll is run and it must be written down
When a payroll workbook is passed on and the next owner needs inputs, steps and risks

tasks.task: Explain a pay change or review outcome to staff

items.when: When a new pay structure needs an announcement, FAQ and manager talking points
When an approved pay policy must be explained in plain words with a rollout list
Before sending, to list the hard questions staff will ask about their own pay
Before sending, to read it as someone who got less than they hoped

tasks.task: Check contractor status and the monthly contractor list

items.when: When someone works like staff but is paid by invoice
Each month, to see who to keep, whose terms to fix and which agreements to redo
When the firm uses many contractors and needs an onboarding list and a vendor plan

always.when: At the start of any sizeable job, to capture the real firm, its country and its written pay rules
Whenever the work states a legal rate, threshold or market figure, to give it a dated source
Before any workbook leaves your hands, to find broken formulas and wrong totals
Before anything goes to staff, to make sure they can follow why they are paid what they are

helpers.when: When payroll must be posted, reconciled to the bank and closed in the books
When a pay question turns into a contract, policy or performance matter
When the pay model or pre-check needs a robust workbook with locked formulas
When commission needs clean deal data, quota history and CRM rules for split deals
When pay bands or a review must fit the yearly budget and forecast
When a pay reporting or transparency rule applies and needs a control check

gaps: No library item checks gross-to-net pay or a payslip line by line; the pre-check items stop at the inputs
No library item reconciles the payroll register to the bank payment file and to tax and pension payments
No library item designs a commission plan with on-target pay, quota from capacity, accelerators and caps; the library only checks plans
No library item builds a commission payout model with scenarios in a spreadsheet
No library item costs benefits options per person at different budget levels
No library item runs an annual pay review with a merit grid and budget split
No library item levels jobs by scope for a small firm; the career ladder item is about growth talks
No library item prepares pay gap or pay transparency reporting
No library item handles a pay error: working out the correction and writing to the employee
No library item builds a payroll calendar with year-end and filing dates by country
No library item writes a full total pay statement or makes different layouts of one to compare
No library item makes different versions of a pay change message to choose between
The library has no tool guide for payroll software or for Excel on its own
